flawed_step: The hypothesis does not force connectedness or a common vertex among distinct triangles.
counterexample: Let V={1,2,3,4,5,6} and E={{1,2},{2,3},{1,3},{4,5},{5,6},{4,6}}. This is the disjoint union of two triangles. Every edge lies in exactly one triangle, but no vertex is adjacent to all five other vertices.
assessment_summary: A disjoint union of two triangles satisfies every hypothesis and has no universal vertex, so the statement is false.
